target.title: feat(scheduler): prioritize exact-review backlog
target.body:
## Summary

- Prioritize only **healthy, target-admissible** exact-review backlog when choosing background review capacity.
- Preserve existing exact-review admission, leases, quotas, and the global worker budget; this change only reduces competing background work while the exact lane is demonstrably saturated.
- Publish `ready_pending` and `admissible_pending` queue telemetry, and log the selected background cap or an explicit fail-open warning in both review schedulers.

## Problem

The dashboard's global fleet capacity and the independently admitted exact-review lane are different resources. A saturated exact-review lane can have accepted work waiting even while the fleet has spare Codex budget. Background issue/PR and commit-review scheduling should yield some capacity in that specific, healthy condition rather than continue competing at its normal rate.

The current base also raises exact-review capacity and completes a lease before state-ledger publication. This PR is complementary: it does not change those queue mechanics, and it does not treat a public snapshot as permission to change admission.

## Implementation

- `dashboard/worker.ts` reports both:
  - `ready_pending`: pending items whose retry time is due;
  - `admissible_pending`: due items that can consume the next global exact-review slot after applying the same target-cap admission rule as the queue.
- `sweep.yml` and `commit-review.yml` classify pressure only when all of these are true:
  - exact lane is full (`dispatching + leased >= capacity`);
  - dispatcher is `active`;
  - handoff health is `healthy`;
  - `admissible_pending > 0`.
- A healthy full lane is `congested` when its admissible backlog is below lane capacity and `saturated` when it meets/exceeds that capacity. The configured background caps are 16 under congestion and 4 under saturation; the existing commit-review default of 6 stays below the congestion cap.
- Missing, malformed, or not-yet-deployed telemetry, retry-delayed work, target-cap-blocked work, paused dispatch, and degraded/stalled handoff all fail open to the normal scheduler behavior. The workflows emit a GitHub Actions warning when queue telemetry cannot be read.

## Validation

Ran from this branch after rebase onto `origin/main` (`3ab249b8c043366ace28f24779e4f2a4e7017853`):

```text
pnpm run build:all
node --test test/repair/workflow-utils.test.ts                         # 48 passed
node --test --test-name-pattern "background review schedulers yield" test/sweep-workflow.test.ts
node --test --test-name-pattern "dashboard status" test/dashboard-worker.test.ts  # 4 passed
pnpm lint repair
pnpm lint scripts
pnpm check:limits
pnpm exec oxfmt --check <the 10 touched files>
git diff --check origin/main...HEAD
```

- The full `test/sweep-workflow.test.ts` suite cannot run on this Windows host because its WSL Bash test helper lacks `/bin/bash`; the focused static scheduler test above passes.
- Docker actionlint was run against the repository. It reports pre-existing warnings/errors outside this PR's changed blocks: `exact-review-reconcile.yml:27`; `sweep.yml:240,527,824,2247,3516`. The last two are legacy `concurrency.queue` schema findings. No actionlint finding points to the changed scheduler blocks.

## Live and decision-table proof

At `2026-07-14T01:06:42Z`, the public status endpoint returned:

```text
generated_at=2026-07-14T01:05:56.953Z
pending=42; dispatching=11; leased=37
dispatcher=active; handoff=stalled
ready_pending=<not present>; admissible_pending=<not present>
```

That is expected before this dashboard change is deployed. Passing the missing `admissible_pending` value and stalled handoff into the compiled scheduler returns `idle`, proving the safe fail-open path; it does not throttle background review from an incomplete or unhealthy public snapshot.

The compiled local decision table returns:

```text
healthy full fixture with 48 admissible pending -> saturated
saturated normal_review cap                   -> 4
saturated hot_intake cap                      -> 4
saturated commit_review cap                   -> 4
stalled or missing-schema fixture             -> idle (fail open)
```

No direct workflow dispatch was used for this proof.

## Codex review closeout

- `codex review --uncommitted` was run during the fix loop; accepted findings were addressed by making pressure depend on queue admission rather than total pending work.
- Final `codex review --base origin/main` on the rebased head completed clean: **"No actionable correctness issues were identified in the changes relative to the specified merge base."**

## Risks and rollout

This is intentionally conservative: it can reduce background review throughput only while a healthy exact-review lane has backlog that is eligible for the next exact slot. It has no token, permission, queue-admission, lease, or state-publication change. Before the dashboard deployment reaches production, missing new telemetry leaves scheduler behavior unchanged.
